free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: Free; uploads served from *.discourse-cdn.com behind CloudFront, so a Cloudflare/CloudFront cache sits in front already

tooling: Discourse's own REST API is fully available on the free site (POST /uploads.json with an API key, /posts.json, /latest.json); no rclone backend
chaining: 5 GB x N free sites. Free sites are self-serve from id.discourse.com/create-site with a Discourse ID; provisioning is rate-limited but per-hour, not per-account. 100 sites = 500 GB; 400 sites = 2 TB.
limits_note: 5 GB per site; 2 staff seats; 10 categories; no tags; no private categories; site provisioning throttled ('You have provisioned too many sites in the past hour'); post/upload rate limits are default Discourse

identity_cost.detail: no identity_cost field and no identity statement in the source record; defaulted to email and flagged, not evidence

reliability_note: Free plan launched 2026-02 and is still labelled beta; the provisioning throttle is the real scaling brake, and the 10-category cap makes bulk-upload workflows awkward.
